name: Steve Jobs
description: A journey through destiny-shaping decisions that forged a life of innovation and ambition — but every choice can lead you to a completely different fate.

scoring.historicalSimilarity: sum of weight for historically matching choices / sum of all event weights * 100
scoring.risk: average risk score of selected choices
scoring.independence: average independence score of selected choices

events.title: An Adopted Child
events.playerFact: Shortly after birth, a family adopts you and raises you in a modest home. From childhood, you have a curious and determined nature.
events.historicalFact: You were born in 1955 and soon after, a family in the San Francisco Bay Area adopted and raised you.
events.question: You have the opportunity to raise an adopted child. Do you accept the responsibility?

yes.consequence: You decide to raise the child and give them a loving home.

no.consequence: You decide not to raise the child. Their life begins with another family.

events.title: A Curious Young Mind
events.playerFact: In your teens, you become fascinated with electronics and computing machines — devices that seem to have endless possibilities. You meet someone who shares this obsession completely.
events.historicalFact: In your teens, you developed a deep interest in electronics and computers, and you found a kindred spirit who became your lifelong collaborator.
events.question: You meet someone who is just as obsessed with electronics as you are. Will you work together?

yes.consequence: You become close friends and start building things together.

no.consequence: You continue exploring electronics on your own, most of the time pursuing your interests alone.

events.title: Dropping Out of College
events.playerFact: You enroll in a liberal arts college but soon feel that formal education is not for you. It's expensive, and your family's finances are strained.
events.historicalFact: You enrolled in Reed College but dropped out after about six months, partly due to financial pressure on your adoptive parents.
events.question: College doesn't feel right for you. Will you drop out and find your own path?

yes.consequence: You leave college and begin exploring life outside the traditional education system.

no.consequence: You stay in college and continue toward a conventional degree.

events.title: The Calligraphy Class
events.playerFact: Even after dropping out of formal education, you continue attending classes that genuinely interest you. One of them is a calligraphy course — the art of beautiful writing. It has no obvious practical application, but it fascinates you.
events.historicalFact: After dropping out of college, you continued taking classes. The calligraphy course you took later influenced your company's revolutionary approach to typography and design.
events.question: A calligraphy class captivates you, even though it has no clear practical value. Will you take it?

yes.consequence: You study calligraphy simply because you are fascinated by it.

no.consequence: You decide calligraphy has little practical value and pass on it.

events.title: Journey to the East
events.playerFact: In your early twenties, you feel drawn to Eastern philosophy. An opportunity arises to travel to a distant land in search of spiritual enlightenment.
events.historicalFact: In your early twenties, you traveled to India in search of spiritual enlightenment — a journey that deeply shaped your worldview and aesthetic sensibility.
events.question: You have the chance to travel to the East in search of spiritual answers. Will you go?

yes.consequence: You travel and explore spirituality and different ways of thinking.

no.consequence: You stay home and focus on technology and work.

events.title: The Game Company
events.playerFact: After returning from your journey, a young video game company offers you a job. The company is small but growing, in an industry that barely exists yet.
events.historicalFact: After returning from India, you worked at Atari and became more deeply involved in the emerging personal computer scene.
events.question: A young game company offers you a job. Will you take this opportunity?

yes.consequence: You join the company and gain experience in the nascent gaming industry.

no.consequence: You turn down the job and look for another path.

events.title: The Computing Machine
events.playerFact: Your friend has built a working computing machine in his spare time. It's a simple device, but you immediately see that it could be more than a hobby. You see an opportunity to build something ordinary people can use.
events.historicalFact: Your collaborator designed a personal computer, and you saw the potential to turn it into a commercial product — a machine anyone could use, not just hobbyists.
events.question: Your friend has built a working computing machine. Will you turn his invention into a joint business?

yes.consequence: You decide the machine can become a real product, and you start a company with your friend.

no.consequence: You decide the machine is more of an interesting hobby than a business opportunity.

events.title: The Polished Version
events.playerFact: Your machine is gaining attention. It's still mostly a device for hobbyists, but you believe it can reach a much broader audience. You want to make it polished, accessible, and beautiful — something people would want in their homes.
events.historicalFact: The second version of your product became a huge success, helping establish your company as a major force in personal computing. It set a new standard for what a personal computer could be.
events.question: Your machine is gaining traction. Will you invest heavily to turn it into a polished consumer product?

yes.consequence: You focus on making the machine accessible, attractive, and successful.

no.consequence: You keep the company focused mainly on technology and hobbyists.

events.title: The Ouster
events.playerFact: Tensions rise within the company you helped build. The leadership you brought in sees things differently. Eventually, you are pushed out of the very organization you founded.
events.historicalFact: After a power struggle with the company's leadership, you were ousted from the business you had founded — a painful but ultimately liberating moment.
events.question: You have lost control of the company you helped build. Will you leave and start something new?

yes.consequence: You leave the company and decide to build the next chapter of your life elsewhere.

no.consequence: You remain determined to regain your influence within the company.

events.title: A Fresh Start
events.playerFact: You have the freedom to build from scratch. You start a new company focused on powerful machines for professionals. Separately, you invest in a small computer graphics team working on something entirely new — storytelling with machines.
events.historicalFact: After leaving the company you founded, you built a new company to create advanced workstations, and you acquired what would become a pioneering animation studio.
events.question: You have the freedom to begin again. Will you start a new computing company and invest in computer animation?

yes.consequence: You start a new company and back a graphics project that will transform both industries.

no.consequence: You choose a quieter path and avoid building another large technology company.

events.title: Life in an Orphanage
events.playerFact: You are not adopted and grow up in an orphanage. Your fate is completely different — you never gain access to technology or electronics, and you live an ordinary life.
events.historicalFact: History is full of stories where one decision changes a life path forever.
events.question: Do you regret not accepting the adoption?

yes.consequence: You die with regret, wishing you had given the child a better chance at life.

no.consequence: You die peacefully, believing you made the right decision — unaware that the world lost a genius.

events.title: Alone Among Machines
events.playerFact: You reject your companion and continue your electronics work alone. You build small projects but never form a powerful partnership.
events.historicalFact: Some talented engineers, due to a lack of collaboration, never turned big ideas into big products.
events.question: Are you satisfied with working alone?

yes.consequence: You become an independent developer, making useful tools, but you never build an empire.

no.consequence: You constantly think about that lost partner, and this regret haunts you for life.

events.title: An Ordinary Graduate
events.playerFact: You stay in college, study, and earn a degree. You become a professor or a clerk, living a quiet life, but you never enter the technology world.
events.historicalFact: Many talented students who stayed on traditional paths never reached their potential.
events.question: Do you regret staying in college?

yes.consequence: You die with regret, wishing you had had the courage to drop out.

no.consequence: You die peacefully, believing education was the best choice — unaware that the world will never know your name.

events.title: Rough Design
events.playerFact: You don't take the calligraphy class and never learn about visual subtlety and typography. Your products always remain rough and unappealing, never excelling in design.
events.historicalFact: Some technology companies, by ignoring design, never achieved market dominance.
events.question: Do you regret not studying calligraphy?

yes.consequence: You die with regret, wishing you had valued aesthetics as well.

no.consequence: You die with pride, believing function is more important than beauty — unaware that design was the key to your competitors' success.

events.title: The Soulless Entrepreneur
events.playerFact: You reject the spiritual journey and focus entirely on business. You become wealthy, but your deep aesthetic and human sensibility never develops.
events.historicalFact: Some successful entrepreneurs, by neglecting spirituality and art, never achieved true genius.
events.question: Do you regret not going on the spiritual journey?

yes.consequence: You die wealthy but with an empty heart, wishing you had cared for your soul as well.

no.consequence: You die with pride, believing pragmatism is better than dreaming — though your products never have soul or unique appeal.

events.title: Lost in the Industry
events.playerFact: You turn down the game company job and drift into scattered work. You never enter the personal computing industry and miss the golden opportunity.
events.historicalFact: The history of industry is full of those who ignored early opportunities and later regretted it.
events.question: Do you regret turning down that job?

yes.consequence: You die with regret, wishing you had paid attention to that early opportunity.

no.consequence: You die peacefully, believing fate had other plans — but you know you missed a big chance.

events.title: The Unknown Inventor
events.playerFact: You don't turn your friend's computing machine into a business. He develops it alone, but without your marketing and vision, it never achieves commercial success.
events.historicalFact: Some great inventions never reached the market due to the lack of a proper entrepreneur.
events.question: Do you regret not turning it into a business?

yes.consequence: You die with regret, wishing you had had the courage to invest in it.

no.consequence: You die peacefully, believing these machines were just hobbies — unaware they would change the world.

events.title: A Product for Elites
events.playerFact: You keep your machine only for hobbyists and specialists. You never think about simplicity and beauty, and your competitors take the consumer market.
events.historicalFact: Some technology companies, by focusing on specialists, lost the massive consumer market.
events.question: Do you regret focusing only on hobbyists?

yes.consequence: You die with regret, wishing you had thought about ordinary people too.

no.consequence: You die with pride, believing your products were for the best — though your company stayed small and the world passed you by.

events.title: The Power Fight
events.playerFact: You don't leave the company and fight to regain control. You spend years in political battles, draining your energy. Eventually, the company collapses, and you go down with it.
events.historicalFact: Some founders, unable to let go, drove their companies to ruin.
events.question: Do you regret fighting for power?

yes.consequence: You die with regret, wishing you had gone your own way and started over instead of fighting.

no.consequence: You die bitterly, believing you were right — but the company died, and you with it.

events.title: A Quiet Life
events.playerFact: After the ouster, you decide to retire from technology. You engage in quieter pursuits and never return to the industry. Years later, your competitors change the world, and you are just a spectator.
events.historicalFact: Some great entrepreneurs, after a failure, never returned, and history passed them by.
events.question: Do you regret retiring early?

yes.consequence: You die with regret, wishing you had had the courage to start over instead of withdrawing.

no.consequence: You die peacefully, believing a quiet life is better than the stress of entrepreneurship — unaware that the world will never remember your name.
